bonus_mechanics: Depreciation follows federal: 2025 Form 2 instructions Sch. I line 19: 'Depreciation, depletion, and amortization deductions must be the same for federal and Montana income tax purposes.' The base is federal taxable income, and no add-back for 168(k) exists in 15-30-2120(2). So 100% bonus for property acquired after 19 Jan 2025 (40% for earlier-acquired property) and the OBBBA 168(n) allowance flow through. Layer check: Rev. Proc. 2024-40 (179 at 1,250,000/3,130,000, 40% bonus) is superseded by P.L. 119-21 sec. 70301/70306/70307.

special_rules: Title plant depreciation/amortization added back (code AG). Federal QBI deduction is NOT allowed for Montana (instructions p. 7). 280E cannabis business expenses are subtractable on Schedule I line 20. Montana NOL transition carryforward (codes AN/SL) is separate from depreciation. 179 is not named in the instruction; its conformity rests on the 'depreciation same as federal' sentence and the federal-income starting point.

bonus_mechanics: Nebraska individual income tax starts from federal AGI. DOR: 'For tax years beginning on and after January 1, 2006, taxpayers are not required to add-back any bonus depreciation or enhanced section 179 expense deduction taken on their federal return.' So the federal bonus flows through unchanged. (The 85% add-back with 20%-a-year subtraction applied only to assets placed in service after 10 Sep 2001 and before 31 Dec 2005.)
special_rules: Only relevant to old assets: property placed in service 2001-2005 carried Nebraska add-backs (85% of bonus; 100% of enhanced 179 for 2003-2005) recovered 20% a year, fully recovered by 2010. Nebraska corporate tax starts from federal taxable income and has no difference noted.

bonus_mechanics: Follows the federal rule. DOR (2 Sep 2025, report under Neb. Rev. Stat. 77-27,222): 'Nebraska is a state of rolling conformity to the federal tax code'; individual calculations begin with federal AGI, so provisions that affect federal AGI 'automatically affect the Nebraska individual income tax'; secs. 70301, 70302, 70306 and 70307 'result in less taxable income for owners of pass-through businesses, effectively lowering Nebraska tax receipts'. So 100% bonus (property acquired and placed in service on or after 20 Jan 2025; 40% earlier), the 179 limit of 2,500,000 / 4,000,000 and the 168(n) allowance flow through for 2025. Layer check: Rev. Proc. 2024-40 amounts (1,250,000 / 3,130,000; 40%) are superseded by P.L. 119-21.

DOR's 2026 legislative changes page lists no depreciation change.

bonus_mechanics: Personal level: not applicable. New Hampshire taxes no wages, and its only personal income-type tax (Interest and Dividends Tax, 5% for periods ending before 31 Dec 2023) reaches interest and dividends only, with no depreciation computation. Business Profits Tax (BPT, RSA 77-A), which does reach sole proprietors (NH-1040), partnerships and corporations: applies the IRC 'without section 168(k)' (RSA 77-A:3-b, I), so NO bonus (0%); regular depreciation under IRC 167/168 therefore differs from the federal return and a separate NH basis is kept.
special_rules: BPT only (entity/business level, not a personal income tax): 179 allowed under RSA 77-A:3-a but capped at 500,000 for property placed in service on or after 1 Jan 2018 (100,000 for 2017 placed-in-service per an NH-1040 instruction excerpt); the phase-out threshold is not stated in any text I could read. BPT ties to the IRC in effect on 31 Dec 2018 (fixed date, periods beginning on or after 1 Jan 2020). Rental income is BPT-reachable only above the gross-business-income filing threshold (threshold not researched).
source_citation: NH DRA: Interest and Dividends Tax repeal (HB 2, 2023) and rates; RSA 77-A:3-a and 77-A:3-b, 77-A:1 XX as excerpted from gc.nh.gov / revenue.nh.gov search results

bonus_mechanics: Gross Income Tax (GIT) depreciation is computed without the federal special depreciation allowance. N.J.S.A. 54A:5-1.2 (P.L. 2004, c.65) decouples assets placed in service on or after 1 Jan 2004. GIT-DEP (Revised 8/19): 'The federal 50% Special Depreciation Allowance is not allowed', and only a 30% allowance 'is allowed only if it was taken for federal tax purposes'. NJ basis = federal basis before special allowance/179/depreciation, less the NJ 179 deduction; NJ depreciation uses the federal method and life. The adjustment (federal depreciation incl. bonus and 179, minus NJ 179, minus NJ depreciation) goes on GIT-DEP line 7 each year until the asset is fully depreciated or disposed of. The forms name only the 30% and 50% rates; they do not mention the 100% (2021) bonus, so 'none' for that rate is the Division's rule applied by inference.
conformity_date: 2002-12-31 (IRC 179 only, per the Division: 179 'calculated pursuant to the federal Internal Revenue Code in effect on December 31, 2002')
special_rules: Max NJ 179 is 25,000 total per income category (net profits from business; rents/royalties) per individual, partnership or S corporation; the federal reduced-dollar limitation applies using 25,000 as the maximum; no business-income limit; unused 179 and unused adjustment cannot be carried forward or back or used against another category. One GIT-DEP per category (e.g., all rental properties on one worksheet). Adjusts 179 recapture income and gain/loss on disposition. If the first NJ adjustment was never reported (error not corrected by the Division, or no NJ filing requirement), NJ basis equals federal basis and no adjustment is required or allowed later. Liberty Zone property: 179 max 60,000. Partnerships and S corporations with an NJ filing requirement compute their own adjustment (NJ-1065 line 13c/15f; CBT-100S Sch K).
source_citation: NJ Division of Taxation, GIT-DEP General Instructions and Parts I-IV (Revised 8/19); N.J.S.A. 54A:5-1.2 (P.L. 2004, c.65); https://www.nj.gov/treasury/taxation/decouples2.shtml
verify_note: GIT-DEP text read in full (Revised 8/19, read from the 2022 and 2024 URL paths; 2021 form not read, same revision assumed). The 200,000 phase-out is derived (IRC 179(b)(2) as in effect 31 Dec 2002, not printed on any NJ form). TCJA bonus rates are not named in the forms. The statute itself was not read.

bonus_mechanics: GIT-DEP Revised 10/25 (the first revision after P.L. 119-21, read in full) keeps the same rules: 'The federal 50% Special Depreciation Allowance is not allowed'; 30% only if taken federally; max NJ 179 'is $25,000'; NJ basis net of NJ 179 only; adjustment on line 8. It says nothing about the OBBBA 100% bonus (acquired after 19 Jan 2025), so 100% is treated as not allowed by the same decoupling (inference). Layer check: neither Rev. Proc. 2024-40 (179 at 1,250,000) nor OBBBA (2,500,000) reaches NJ, because NJ's 25,000 is statutory.
change_note: 10/25 GIT-DEP adds Part II(a), an alternate depreciation deduction for certain new affordable housing developments (tax years beginning on or after 1 Jan 2025; construction begins on or after 20 Mar 2024). No change to 179, bonus or the 25,000 cap. 168(n) (OBBBA qualified production property) is not mentioned: Part II still bases NJ depreciation on the federal method and life with no special allowance, so none is allowed in effect, but this is unconfirmed.
special_rules: Alternate depreciation (affordable housing, 2025+): at least 20% of units affordable; property taxes not abated or exempted under the Long Term Tax Exemption Law; no affordable-housing construction subsidy; deductible percentage = (affordable units / total units) x 2 of eligible capital expenditures, depreciated over 10 years with the federal method (Part II(a) column I 'Use 10-year life'); adjustment = federal depreciation less NJ alternate depreciation, on line 5. Otherwise as 2021 (25,000 cap per category, no carryforward, one GIT-DEP per category, non-reporter rule).
